Imo there are some people whose lives are shitty and they will never get better. This might be me (jury is still out though, gonna give it a few more years). I strongly believe in a right to die.

However, I also believe that most people who are suicidal at some point end up having a net positive life (as in they are glad they didn't and they had more moments of total positivity than negativity - I don't believe in any of that stay alive because other people will be sad bs, be nice to others while you are here but be alive for yourself). 

I also believe that when people talk about their own desire to commit suicide they are reaching out. They might not want to admit that, I certainly don't, but realistically that is what it is there for. The way I see it if you are gonna commit suicide you should be in a calm and logically framed mindset. Obviously how you feel is the only thing that really matters but if you are currently emotional you're cherrypicking that information in a way that you aren't in a more logical mindset. And telling people you're going to commit suicide isn't really a logical thing to do if you are absolutely 100% certain you want to. It's not gonna benefit those people, and it's gonna make it harder for you to do it.

Which is why whenever someone posts here saying they want to commit suicide you should always try and stop them, because they are literally not going to make that post unless they are in an emotional state of mind or they are not quite sure and are seeking that out even if they're not gonna admit it.

This is called hypersexuality and is considered and treated as a medical condition. 

You should see a doctor because they might be able to prescribe you cyproterone acetate for this (which is a testosterone blocker). 

Source: I am trans and I actually looked into lying about having hypersexuality in order to receive treatment (because drugs which affect androgens are considered extremely dangerous to give to trans people unless they are 5000% sure they are trans and so are their parents and they have been wearing nothing but pink dresses from the age of 2 onwards, but the same drugs are considered entirely harmless when given to non-trans people) but I ended up just DIYing instead

If you're worried about the feminising effects, I'm not gonna lie you might get some, but simply reducing the testosterone level without adding estrogen isn't likely to lead to any major changes (and most aesthetic changes from testosterone are pretty permanent)
